subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw keep Codex models on the app-server and pursue the app-server/upstream 429 cause, or make the direct OpenClaw runtime a supported Codex path by adding Harmony tool-call parsing?
rationale: The choice changes runtime ownership, provider fallback behavior, and tool-call parsing semantics; source inspection shows both paths are plausible but not safe for automation to choose without maintainer intent and live Codex proof.

options.title: App-server first
options.body: Finish and review the model-scoped auth-profile fix, keep app-server as the default, and require live proof of the suspected upstream 429/websocket behavior before changing routing.

options.title: Direct Harmony adapter
options.body: Add Codex Harmony `to=functions.*` parsing to the direct OpenAI Responses runtime, then evaluate explicit direct-runtime fallback for Codex OAuth models.

options.title: Wait for stronger live proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer-owned live repro captures the app-server request, direct sibling success, and fallback decision trace together.

recommendation.title: App-server first
recommendation.body: Finish and review the model-scoped auth-profile fix, keep app-server as the default, and require live proof of the suspected upstream 429/websocket behavior before changing routing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex model support, and the direct AI runtime surface affected by the decision.
